claims.statement: `web/src/api/` is a handwritten typed client marked as such by `API_CLIENT_ORIGIN = 'handwritten'`, whose `request<T>` primitive calls the relative `/api` base, rethrows non-2xx responses as an `ApiError` carrying `status` and `detail`, and resolves `204` without parsing a body; the Vite dev proxy forwards `/api` to `API_HTTP`/`API_HTTPS` or falls back to `http://localhost:5192`.

`api.getLabel(id, includeReleases)` only appends `?includeReleases=false`, and `api.getLabelReleases(id, page, pageSize)` always sends both `page` and `pageSize`, which is what selects the backend's paged response envelope.

The SPA's DTO types in `web/src/api/types.ts` are hand-maintained mirrors of the contract rather than generated ones, so they both omit backend fields the SPA ignores (`slug`, `updatedAt`, `labelSpotify`) and shape the paged feed as `LabelReleasesPage` / `AlbumSummary`; switching to the generated client via `npm run generate:client` is scoped to keeping the `/api` base path and the `ApiError` shape stable.

`/labels/:id` is a lazy route with `props: true`, so `LabelDetailView` re-runs `load()` through `watch(() => props.id, load, { immediate: true })` when the id changes rather than reusing a cached view.

All paging state for the label detail feed is component-local `ref`s in `LabelDetailView.vue`; the Pinia labels store holds only followed-label summaries and caches no release data, and because `store.fetchLabels()` is only triggered by `LabelsView`, a direct load of a label detail can start with an empty store and therefore no "Following" badge.

The initial label detail load fires `api.getLabel(id, false)` and `api.getLabelReleases(id, 1, PAGE_SIZE)` concurrently in one `Promise.all` with a page size of 5, so the detail request stays a single query and the releases arrive through the paged endpoint instead.

The label detail page has four mutually exclusive render states driven by the load outcome: a skeleton while loading, an `EmptyState` for a `404`, an `ErrorState` whose retry event re-invokes `load()` for any other failure, and the header plus Releases/Artists tabs on success, where the Artists tab is fed from the unpaged `detail.artists` list.

The load outcome is classified by duck-typing a `status` property on the thrown error (`err instanceof Error && 'status' in err`) rather than testing `instanceof ApiError`, so the `ApiError` shape promised by `http.ts` - not the class identity - is the contract a view actually depends on; the 404 branch also covers a malformed non-GUID id because the backend constrains the route segment.

`loadMore()` is guarded on `loadingMore || !hasMore`, requests `currentPage + 1` at the same page size, and a failed page fetch does not clear `hasMore` or advance `currentPage` - it raises a `vue-sonner` error toast so the same page can simply be retried.

Each merged page overwrites `currentPage`, `totalCount` and `hasMore` from the response envelope, so the view trusts the server's `hasMore` (`page * pageSize < totalCount`) instead of counting locally.

`mergeReleasePages` appends only releases whose album `id` is not already loaded and keeps the already loaded copy on a collision, absorbing the page overlap the backend creates when the background poller inserts new albums at the top of the newest-first list between two page fetches.

Rendering order is produced client-side by a `sortedReleases` computed that re-sorts merged pages with `releaseSortKey`, which normalises `year`/`month` precision to the first day of the period and maps a missing date to `0000-01-01`; `AlbumCard` renders the same precision through `formatReleaseDate`.

The header's release count is `loadedReleases.length` and its artist count is `countUniqueArtists(loadedReleases)`, the number of distinct credited artist *names* across loaded releases - not artist ids and not the label's linked artists - so both grow as pages are revealed and both differ by design from the accurate `artistCount`/`releaseCount` the detail response carries but this view never renders.

The new-releases badge counts `page.totalCount` growth against the `initialTotalCount` baseline captured from the first page, is shown only while `newReleasesCount > 0 && loadedReleases.length < totalCount` (suppressed once everything is loaded), and is cleared by clicking it, which calls `resetPaging()` and reloads from page one with a fresh baseline instead of merging just the new rows.

`load()` and `loadMore()` each keep their own monotonic sequence counter and discard any response whose token is no longer current, making fast navigation between label details safe on the load path in the same defensive style as the Pinia store's `fetchId`/`revision` guards.

The two guards in `LabelDetailView` are not linked: `load()` resets paging and clears `loadingMore` but never bumps `loadMoreRequest`, so an in-flight page-N+1 response for the previous label still passes its own guard after a navigation and is merged into the freshly reset list together with the previous label's `currentPage` and `hasMore`; bumping `loadMoreRequest` during reset would close it without touching the pure helpers.

Paging logic is deliberately split so the behaviour is testable: the view delegates merging and artist counting to the pure `web/src/utils/paging.ts` helpers, whose only consumers are `LabelDetailView` and `web/src/utils/paging.test.ts`.

`web/src/utils/paging.test.ts` is the only frontend unit test file; it covers `mergeReleasePages` (disjoint append, overlap de-duplication, and the already loaded copy winning a collision) and `countUniqueArtists` (name de-duplication, zero for an empty list, one for a single-artist label), with no component test for the counters, the badge baseline, or the guards.
The web CI workflow runs `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` for pull requests against `main` and does not run `npm test`, so the vitest paging unit tests are not enforced in CI today.
